fields.quoted_span: For new tenancies, the Guide must be provided when a tenant signs a lease or enters into a tenancy agreement for the first time or tenders the first month’s rent. The Ordinance also requires that a landlord provide the Guide to tenants when legal steps to terminate a tenancy are taken (ex. Notice to Quit or Summary Process).
fields.note: All elements are in the FAQ: all tenants and lawful occupants, tenants at will, no renewal requirement, no signed receipt, eviction not barred, $300 per day, and the Guide offered at the same time as the notice.

fields.quoted_span: You may be fined $300 for each day’s violation.
fields.note: The Guide at tenancy start and with a notice to quit or summary process is supported by the timing FAQ. The $300 daily fine is also supported.
The field is empty and the document gives no adoption or effective date. Only page posting and modification dates appear.

fields.quoted_span: The Ordinance requires owners, landlords, and management companies to provide you with information at the start of your lease or tenancy as well as when your tenancy is being terminated.
fields.note: The page describes the ordinance in the present tense as operative, which supports in_force. It does not state the status explicitly.

fields.quoted_span: Yes, the Ordinance applies to a residential rental agreements, including single residential dwelling unit.
fields.note: The exemptions for hospitals, skilled nursing and health facilities, non-profit substance-abuse facilities, and Short Term Rental Units under Zoning Art. 4 § 4.60 are all stated. Tenancies at will are covered. The single-unit owner-occupant point is also supported.
